title: Carried-Charge Anchor Date Decision Table for Closed Electric Service Agreements
content:
**Electric Service Agreement — closed agreements.** The carried-charge anchor date is the date from which the calendar days of the carried late payment charge are counted up to the transfer day when a closed agreement's unpaid balance is transferred. It is chosen by the closed agreement's history.

## Decision table

| A payment on the closed agreement reversed as returned unpaid in the 12 calendar months before the transfer | Final bill issued 6 or more calendar days after the agreement's stop date | Carried-charge anchor date |
|---|---|---|
| 1 or more such reversals | either | the final bill's bill date |
| none | yes | the agreement's stop date |
| none | no (5 days or fewer after the stop date) | the final bill's due date |

A returned payment is a payment on the closed agreement that was reversed as returned unpaid; one such reversal in the look-back is enough for the first row.

## Counting the look-back

Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date. The posting here is the transfer.

- Hypothetical: transfer dated 15 September; a payment reversal dated 15 September of the previous year is exactly 12 whole calendar months earlier and is not counted.
- Hypothetical: a payment reversal dated 16 September of the previous year is less than 12 whole calendar months earlier and is counted.

## Stop-date boundary (hypothetical, no returned payment)

- Stop date 3 March, final bill dated 9 March: issued 6 days after the stop date, so the anchor is the stop date.
- Stop date 3 March, final bill dated 8 March: issued 5 days after the stop date, so the anchor is the final bill's due date.
